articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Shojo anime continues to dominate upcoming seasonal anime rotations , with breakout hits like Firefly Wedding becoming viral sensations, as well as fans spinning rumors regarding which new series will be getting a sequel first. Luckily for many, Tamon's B-side , a new shojo anime that originally debuted in December 2025 is finally returning with a second season sometime in the future. Following a live fan event in Tokyo called F/ACE FIRST LIVE "NAUTICAL STAR," it was officially announced that the idol-centric will finally be coming back, with the show's official X (formerly Twitter) uploading a short teaser trailer to share the news.

While there have been no dates given regarding when fans will be able to hear additional details or when the second season will release , it's likely that the same production team from J.C.STAFF that worked on Tamon's B-Side Season 1 will be returning. Season 1 was directed by Chika Nagaoka, best known for her previous work on Case Closed , with series composition and scripts from Chiaki Nagai who previously worked on Horimiya , another massive romance series. Check out the announcement teaser below.

🎊✨ TVアニメ「多聞くん今どっち！？」 第2期製作決定！！ ✨🎊 たくさんの応援、本当にありがとうございます！ 引き続き #多聞くん今どっち を よろしくお願いします！🫶 pic.twitter.com/oAv5XMDjk7

Tamon's B-side explores an extremely popular but surprisingly niche ship dynamic between two characters, focusing entirely on the budding romantic relationship between an idol and their "stan" — a slang term used to describe an extremely enthusiastic and dedicated fan to a person, character, or piece of media. The anime follows a high school-aged housekeeper named Utage Kinoshita who started working part-time to help fund her love for F/ACE, her favorite idol group. While working, she stumbles into a situation where she discovers that her favorite member of the group, Tamon Fukuhara, whose stage persona is boisterous and confident, is actually extremely timid and prone to spiraling into dramatic episodes fueled by his own self doubt.

The series immediately became a hit with shojo fans in part because of the anime's gorgeous animation which turned each member of F/ACE into a bishonen dream as well as its earnest humor and genuinely adorable romance between Utage and Tamon. The pair's relationship develops gradually throughout the first season with Utage working as his personal housekeeper. Instead of her interest in the idol waning because of his "real self," she instead becomes an anchor to help support him in his day-to-day life both on and off stage. The premise for Tamon's B-side feels like something plucked directly from an old school boy band fan fiction and lands perfectly every single episode.

Based on an original manga written by Yuki Shiwasu, Tamon's B-side began publishing in the famous shojo magazine Hana to Yume in 2021. The series is still ongoing, and as of writing, currently has seventeen collected volumes in print. Viz Media publishes the manga in English and currently has thirteen volumes available in both print and digital. While there's still no confirmation when new details regarding the second season of Tamon's B-side will release, it's likely to begin adapting Rintaro's story arc which reveals the true personality of one of F/ACE's other members.

The first season of Tamon's B-side released in December 2025, running for thirteen episodes which adapted the first 33-chapters of the manga. Crunchyroll picked up and currently hosts the anime adaptation on their streaming service for global audiences. When the anime initially began airing, the manga had roughly 1.75-million copies in circulation which jumped to 3.5-million by the time the first season came to an end.

Tamon's B-side has been nominated for multiple manga awards in that time as well, and as of writing is still publishing new chapters, meaning that there's still plenty more of Utage and Tamon for fans of the series to look forward to in the future. Are you excited for Season 2? Let us know in the comments!

articles.title: 5 Diablo Classes From Past Entries That Need to Return in Diablo 5
articles.summary: Courtesy of Blizzard Entertainment The core to building characters in the Diablo series is their class, meaning that fans are wondering which archetypes will be coming to Diablo 5, the next entry in the top-down action RPG series. Although Diablo 5 is still a long time away from releasing, Blizzard has announced the first three classes coming to the […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The core to building characters in the Diablo series is their class, meaning that fans are wondering which archetypes will be coming to Diablo 5 , the next entry in the top-down action RPG series. Although Diablo 5 is still a long time away from releasing, Blizzard has announced the first three classes coming to the game - the Plague Knight, the Monk, and the Demon Hunter. Two of those classes are ones from Diablo 3 , hinting that more fan-favorite character options could come back from throughout the dark fantasy franchise.

Currently, Blizzard has Diablo 5 slated for a 2029 release window, meaning that players will have to wait a considerable time before getting to see any character classes in action. Blizzard has promised that Diablo 5 will have "the largest class roster to date" upon launch, likely building off the expanded class list in Diablo 4 with archetypes like the Spiritborn, Paladin, and Warlock. Should Diablo 5 have a huge character class list for players to pick from, it would give players huge amounts of variety, but also nostalgia if Blizzard brings back some fan-favorite options.

The world of Diablo 5 is said to be a version of Sanctuary that has been set ablaze and destroyed by Diablo himself, turning the land into a hellish wasteland. This dystopian version of the world lends itself to the Plague Knight or Demon Hunter classes, but the Crusader or Paladin would be welcome saviors in such a setting too. From various Diablo games, Crusaders and Paladins have extremely similar playstyles, being defensive tanks with hard-hitting abilities powered by holy magic. There are some subtle differences, but for all intents and purposes, players would be eager to see either of these classes make an appearance in another Diablo .

Having a Paladin or Crusader class be part of the base roster for Diablo 5 would be a new shift for the archetypes too, as they tend to be inclusions much later in a Diablo game's life cycle. For example, the Crusader was a DLC class for Diablo 3 , while Diablo 4 didn't add the Paladin until a big post-launch expansion. Crusaders are masters of Shields and holy magic to stun foes, using a more defensive play style, while Paladins are more aggressive, with heavier weapons to deal high damage to single targets. Players might have their preferences, but perhaps the Paladin's recent existence in Diablo 4 makes the Crusader more likely to appear in the next game.

Currently, the roster for Diablo 5 's classes doesn't have a dedicated archetype tied to magic, even if the Plague Knight will have some supernatural powers over pestilence. While the Wizard, Druid, or Witch Doctor could all be valid classes to revive for the game, I'd argue that the Sorcerer is the most iconic one you almost can't have a Diablo title without. The Sorcerer is a class that has existed in the series since the very first Diablo , representing a key type of character players can create. Out of all the classes that could return, the Sorcerer is organized perhaps the best to fit whatever RPG systems change going into Diablo 5 .

The Sorcerer has powers over Fire, Cold, and Lightning, marking a study into elemental magics for maximum DPS rather than the Wizard's versatility or the Necromancer's AoE spells. Having these studies of magic gives players three paths to go down when making a Sorcerer character, leading to an open door of possibilities when it comes to builds. Players can typically invest completely into something like Fire, tapping into the benefits of burn damage and AoE effects, or try to mix spells together to deal with different situations. One Sorcerer may rely on high mobility through an investment in Lightning and Cold, while another dips into Fire and Lightning for raw damage potential or crowd control.

There are many ways to build a Sorcerer in every Diablo , but the class is also a good pick due to how their variety also extends to gear. Sorcerers tend to use a Staff and light armor, going for statistic advantages to their Mana resource rather than raw physical might. Even the Monk, who doesn't use as much gear as other armored classes, tends to rely on weapon variety and damage calculations, while Sorcerers focus more on making their spells more potent. Every Diablo game needs a glass cannon, and the Sorcerer can easily fulfill that role again in Diablo 5 .

The Necromancer is a classic Diablo 2 class that has popped up in many of the series' games, appearing in every title expect the first one. Even Diablo Immortal , the mobile game, has a Necromancer class, so it would make sense for Diablo 5 to continue that trend. However, for players who may not want to see the Necromancer again, it's worth noting why this class has been so prevalent, and the niche role it creates for players to take on. The Necromancer is obviously special for how it lets players summon hordes of undead allies, creating a fun swarm play style that other classes don't really offer.

Necromancers excel in creating AoE spells to trap and control crowds, letting their minions clean up enemies the rest of the time. The darker setting of Diablo 5 could lend itself to the Necromancer's aesthetic, as the dystopian world likely has plenty of dead bodies around to give the Necromancer some friends. Much like the Sorcerer, the Necromancer can build themselves up in various ways too, investing in blood, bone, or shadow magic to create a variety of builds. Themes around self-preservation, stun effects, or raw damage are all available to players, as long as they can manage the Necromancer's Essence resource.

While some players might wish for the Wizard or Warlock to take up the "sinister" spellcaster role in Diablo 5 , the Necromancer doesn't step on the toes of other classes with its abilities. The Necromancer is wildly different from someone like the Sorcerer, even if they both use magic. The gear pieces of skulls, bones, and scythes are also quite different from tools used by other classes, making the look of the Necromancer different too. For Diablo 5 to stand out, the Necromancer could be the biggest fan-favorite to return, pairing well with the Demon Hunter or Plague Knight for its taboo nature.

Diablo 4 's final class for its last expansion is the Amazon, coming to the game in 2027 according to information shared by Blizzard. This is a female-only character class that hasn't been seen in Diablo since the series' second game, creating a rare archetype that most players are unfamiliar with. This extremely disciplined, athletic, and highly-trained warrior is meant to be a jack-of-all-trades of sorts, excelling as a weapons master proficient with bows, spears, javelins, and crossbows. This sort of mid to longe-range melee fighting style isn't represented much in the Diablo games, so the Amazon could be another great option for Diablo 5 's roster.

If Blizzard is promising more classes than ever before for Diablo 5 , having a slightly limited class like the Amazon wouldn't feel too restrictive either. The Amazon's blueprint from Diablo 4 can be brought over if players end up liking it enough, especially as they dig into the build paths Blizzard has shared for the Amazon so far. Apparently, the Amazon can invest into the following pathways to define how she plays:

Any of these paths existing in Diablo 5 would be incredibly fun to play, marking an easy transition of the Diablo 4 version of the class to the next game. In fact, Blizzard can use the Amazon in Diablo 4 as a testing ground for iterations of the class to come in the following title. The mythical status of this class would help it stand out from more generic ones like the Sorcerer or Barbarian if they get added, while once again bringing some much-needed variety to Diablo 5 .

The Bard has not been playable in a Diablo game since the 1996 classic that started it all, being an attempt to translate a beloved fantasy tabletop archetype into the RPG. The Bard in the first Diablo was a master of dual-wielding weapons but also existed as a jack-of-all-trades for nearly every skill in the game. Diablo 5 could re-invent the Bard entirely, making them reflect their origins as an archetype that draws magic from music and the arts, creating the type of character desperately needed in dark times. Considering how devoid of life and sound Diablo 5 's world seems to be, perhaps the Bard is the hero they require most.

The Bard will likely need a total rework, changing abilities to match Diablo 's evolving design philosophies from over the years. This is exciting, though, as it creates nearly endless possibilities for the class to become something entirely new compared to the others. For example, Blizzard could lean into a Bard's flair for melee attacks, making them wield rapiers or short swords rather than the maces or greatswords of heavier classes. On the other hand, a Bard may rely totally on their musical magic, creating custom songs to provide buffs to allies or debuffs to enemies.

The many directions the Bard could take makes it an interesting challenge for Blizzard designers to bring back should they choose to do so. The Diablo series has many great classes that can go through gameplay overhauls besides the Bard too, correcting "mistakes" of the past for diverse character choices. Yet, Diablo 5 's class list should be full of at least a few from prior games, returning as nostalgic ways to create beloved characters in a new setting.

What character class do you want to see return the most in Diablo 5 ? Let us know in the comments below!

Viewers of the second season of The Hunting Wives , currently streaming on Netflix, will find a poignant message at the end of the season finale: "In Loving Memory of Salli Newman ."

Newman was the senior vice president of television production at Lionsgate, producer of The Hunting Wives . She died of a heart attack on December 8, 2025, in her Burbank home at the age of 67, according to her family.

Hunting Wives showrunner Rebecca Cutter told Entertainment Weekly that Newman died during the filming of Season 2. “So we dedicated the final episode to her," Cutter said. Newman moved to Los Angeles after graduating from Montana State University and launched her show business career at 19, training as an actor and stuntwoman while working as a secretary/assistant at Consolidated Film Industries.

"Salli soaked up all the knowledge she could from industry veterans," her family notes, "and worked hard to learn her craft. articles.title: ‘A Girl Unknown,’ ‘Crawling Into Myself,’ ‘Concrete Land’ Take Main Prizes at Doha Film Festival
articles.summary: Zou Jing’s “A Girl Unknown,” Asmahan Bkerat’s “Concrete Land” and Hamad Al-Fayhani’s “Crawling Into Myself” won the top prizes at the sophomore edition of the revamped Doha Film Festival, which took place between Nov. 19-27 in the Qatari capital. articles.content:
Zou Jing’s “A Girl Unknown,” Asmahan Bkerat’s “Concrete Land” and Hamad Al-Fayhani’s “Crawling Into Myself” won the top prizes at the sophomore edition of the revamped Doha Film Festival , which took place between Nov. 19-27 in the Qatari capital.

Prizes totaled over $300,000, with winners split across four main competition sections: International Feature Film Competition, International Short Film Competition, Made in Qatar Competition and the Ajyal Film Competition for youth aged 16-25, in addition to the inaugural FIPRESCI Prize. “A Girl Unknown,” which won Best Narrative Feature in International Competition, trails a young Chinese girl passed between three families between the ages of 6 and 18; “Crawling Into Myself,” the winner of the Made in Qatar competition, tells the story of a man grappling with a rare illness that erases his facial features. "Concrete Land," the Best Documentary in International Competition, is a multi-generational portrait of a mixed-race family fighting displacement and hostility in Jordan. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Cannes Condemns Five-Year Prison Sentence Against Iranian Palme d’Or Winner Jafar Panahi and Pleads for International Support Sweden’s Oscar Entry 'Adult Supervision' Closes Further Deals (EXCLUSIVE)

Fatma Hassan Alremaihi, festival director and CEO of the Doha Film Institute, said: “Tonight, as we celebrate the winners of the 2026 Doha Film Festival, we celebrate far more than cinematic achievement. We recognize the power of stories to transcend borders, challenge perspectives and bring the experiences of people and communities into the global conversation.”

The festival director added that the Doha Film Institute “believes that important voices deserve to be seen, heard and recognized.”

“The Doha Film Festival exists to provide that platform—bringing together filmmakers and audiences from across the world, championing bold and independent storytelling, and creating space for stories that might otherwise go untold,” she added. “The films we honor tonight remind us that cinema is not simply a reflection of the world we live in; it is a force that can shape how we understand it, connect with one another and imagine a more empathetic future.” blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

This year’s jury at the Qatari festival was presided over by Japanese director Naomi Kawase, who chose the winners alongside French Tunisian actor Adam Bessa, influential Tunisian producer Dora Bouchoucha, visionary Italian documentary filmmaker Gianfranco Rosi and award-winning Palestinian filmmaker and artist Kamal Aljafari.

The short film competition jury was presided over by French Moroccan producer Karim Aitouna, who was joined by Malaysian filmmaker Amanda Nell Eu, and Swiss-Rwandan actress and filmmaker Kayije Kagame. The Made in Qatar jury was led by Lebanese actress and filmmaker Yumna Marwan along with Qatari filmmaker Al Johara Al Thani and Palestinian Belgian filmmaker and producer Naël Khleifi.

The ceremony, which was hosted by Sudanese filmmaker and presenter Amjad Al-Nour, was attended by names such as Elia Suleiman, Brigitte Lacombe and Ahmed Al Baker. Other notable guests included H.E. Sheikha Al-Mayassa bint Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani, chairperson of DFI; H.E. Sheikh Dr. Abdulla bin Ali Al Thani, managing director and vice chairman of the board of directors of Qatar Leadership Centre; Hamad Omar Al-Mannai, chief executive officer of Media City Qatar; and Eng. Abdulaziz Ali Al Mawlawi, chief executive officer of Visit Qatar.

Earlier in the week, the festival delivered a successful industry sidebar, the Doha Industry Days. The three-day event was attended by some 450 prominent executives from 38 countries. Speakers included “Squid Game” creator Hwang Dong-hyuk, “Avengers” director Joe Russo, Omar Sy and Noomi Rapace.

articles.summary: GOG has made a 2021 survival RPG free for all PC users with an account. The PC game in question normally runs at $17.99, but for the next two days and 18 hours, from the moment of writing this, it is 100% free to download. In other words, if claimed before November 30, GOG users […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google GOG has made a 2021 survival RPG free for all PC users with an account. The PC game in question normally runs at $17.99, but for the next two days and 18 hours, from the moment of writing this, it is 100% free to download. In other words, if claimed before November 30, GOG users can permanently add it to their libraries for free. This is notably the first free game GOG has given away for the month of November, and it could end up being the final free game on GOG in 2026.

In addition to a free download for a classic 1998 PC game , all GOG users right now can download developer Silent Dreams' and publisher Headup's 2021 zombie survival RPG, also known as Dead Age 2 . This zombie survival RPG has amassed 1,164 user reviews on Steam to date and 27 on GOG. On Steam, 75% of these user reviews are positive. Meanwhile, on GOG, it has a 3.2 out of 5 stars. These aren't eye-catching scores, but they are decent. Those who have never experienced the game, primarily inspired by The Walking Dead , old-school Fallout games, and Darkest Dungeon , can now remedy, if they so please, this without spending a dime.

While this is a sequel to 2016's Dead Age , the aforementioned pair note that "no knowledge of the previous storyline necessary" to play the newer of the two games. That said, where the original starts at the beginning of a zombie apocalypse, the sequel is set 10 years later, picking up after Jack and his camp flee Freedom City, where a cure for the zombie plague has been developed. Such news creates instability, and now various factions are fighting for control.

50-Hour Survival RPG Those who do decide to check out Dead Age 2 will be getting a lot of content for free. Just to mainline the game takes about 50 to 60 hours. Of course, anything beyond this completion-wise only takes the final hour count higher. This is a lot of content, especially for the price, but it's not uncommon for turn-based old-school RPGs to be lengthy. In fact, it's the norm.

" Dead Age 2 is a very fun zombie survival/turn based RPG that will provide you with hours of entertainment if you enjoy the turn-based old-school RPG format," reads the top-voted user review for the game on Steam. "The game improves on practically everything the first game did. A great sequel by devs who obviously care very much about their game."

Meanwhile, the negative reviews that exist, they are the minority, but they all share common complaints, noting the game is grindy, has several optimization issues, and generally has some tedious design flaws.

articles.title: I Didn’t Expect Hexed To Leave Me With A Question Involving Disney Princesses
articles.summary: This was unexpected!
articles.content:
Spoilers for Disney's Hexed are ahead! You can catch the movie in theaters now.

Let me back up a bit, though. Hexed centers on Billie Doe, a mischievous high school student with a heart of gold who discovers she has magical powers while trying to evade her principal, who is going to expel her. Back at home, Billie opens a portal to Hexe, the magic-filled world where witches and wizards live. It’s there that she meets the Queen of Hexe, who just so happens to be her grandmother. Now, I’m not an expert on royal lineage, but I’m pretty sure being the granddaughter of the queen makes you a princess.

There’s no doubt that Billie has met the big four requirements. However, there is one more lesser-known requirement that has to be met for the House of Mouse to consider a character an official princess: the movie has to be a hit. In fact, the success of a movie has to extend well past its release to ensure a princess keeps her title — just look at The Hunchback of Notre Dame’s Esmerelda, who used to be in the official lineup and now is not.

articles.title: 5 Star Wars Legends Starfighters That Can Destroy Anything in Canon
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Lucasfilm Star Wars's original trilogy ended in 1983, but Star Wars was still everywhere until 1986 (I remember because I was still having Star wars figures bought for me until then; Powers of the Force line with character coins). It would fade away for several years, but that would change in the early '90s, when LucasArts […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Star Wars 's original trilogy ended in 1983, but Star Wars was still everywhere until 1986 (I remember because I was still having Star wars figures bought for me until then; Powers of the Force line with character coins). It would fade away for several years, but that would change in the early '90s, when LucasArts started licensing out Star Wars for novels, comics, video games, and role-playing games. This was the beginning of the first Expanded Universe, what we now know as Star Wars Legends . Legends began in 1991, with Star Wars: Dark Empire and Star Wars: Heir to the Empire (people always try to pretend that Star Wars: The Glove of Darth Vader series is somehow Legends canon, mostly to invalidate it in arguments, but it never was), and lasted 31 years, when Disney purchased Lucasfilm in 2012.

Legends of course used the designs from the films, but also created numerous ships and vehicles, including some of the coolest starfighters ever. In fact, the best Legends starfighters are vastly superior to their canon cousins. Canon has some awesome fighters but these Star Wars Legends fighters would waste all of them.

Star Wars has some amazingly lethal starfighters , but every fan knows that the X-Wing is the most dangerous of them. Designed by Incom as the next space superiority fighter, it was too expensive for the Empire, but the Rebels were able to steal the plans and build them. There have been numerous X-Wings variants over the years, its robust space frame, efficient shields, four laser cannons, and two proton torpedo launchers making it a force to reckoned with. It was a favorite of the Jedi and eventually, Incom decided to make a version of the fighter that was created specifically for them.

The StealthX was a heavily modified XJ-3. Its lines were smoothed and the hull was painted black and speckled, meant to blend in with the starfield around. The engines had special bafflers and the ships emissions were basically nil. They also didn't have comms and their sensor systems were extremely limited. Jedi were able to use the Force to make up for all of this, mastering the "shadow bomb" technique (using the Force to push an armed proton torpedo from the launcher, making it completely invisible to instruments). A regular pilot could fly the ship, but it would take someone with the skill of Wedge Antilles or Tycho Celchu to be able to match a Jedi pilot in one. A StealthX would destroy anything in canon before they even knew it was there.

So, a lot of people just scrolled down to this one and are about to rage quit the article, because the Sun Crusher is one of the most ridiculous ships in Star Wars . In fact, it's only technically a starfighter, but it does count. It was created at the secret Maw Installation, an Imperial weapons research facility inside a cluster of black holes. It was the brainchild of Qwi Xux, who was able to invent both its nigh-impenetrable armor and its centerpiece, the nova torpedo launcher. It fired energy projectiles that would cause a chain reaction, causing a star to go supernova, destroying the whole solar system.

The Sun Crusher made the Death Star look quaint. It was armed with five laser cannon turrets, but those were basically worthless. The fighter size vessel could just fly through whatever is in front of it, something it did against an Imperial -class Star Destroyer that was chasing it down. It's armor was powerful enough to take a blast from the Death Star prototype superlaser, but the ship was destroyed when it was flown into a black hole to stop the Empire from getting their hands on it. It's basically the ultimate "Well, mine is better because…" fighter, which is definitely annoying, but since it works, it's fine.

The Yuuzhan Vong made the Empire look quaint . They came from another galaxy, where a race of droids destroyed almost all life. They were able to fight back using their living technology, gaining a burning hatred for any machinery, worshiping their brutal gods. They bred various types of creatures, each that was the equivalent of various standard technology, and made different types of ships, from the massive worldships to the diminutive Yorik-Et Coralskippers. Coralskippers were some of the first Yuuzhan Vong vessels encountered by the New Republic and they immediately made a huge impression.

The fighters were armed with volcano cannons, which allowed them to fire blasts of superheated plasma, and dovin basals. The dovin basal was a heart-shaped organism that manipulated gravity fields, acting as both propulsion and defense for the skips, using voids to suck in lasers and ordinance. Their hulls were made of yorik coral and were extremely dense, making them hard nuts to crack. Eventually, New Republic fighter aces mastered ways around the dovin basals, modifying their cannons to fire "splinter shots" that tired out the dovin basal before using a full power blast to destroy the defenseless skip, allowing them to even up the odds. Canon fighters wouldn't have the same modifications, so the coralskippers would cut through them like butter.

The Mandalorians are known as the most martial race in the galaxy. They've been nomadic warriors for millennia, fighting wars for the highest bidder and then moving on (they also ended up fighting alongside the Sith a lot). In the days after the Yuuzhan Vong War, Mand'alor Boba Fett commanded Mandos to go home to Mandalore and rebuild, leading to the discovery of a huge vein of beskar . The Imperials stripped mine the planet for the ore and the Mandos thought they exhausted the supply decades ago. Suddenly, the Mandos had back one of the most important parts of their old arsenal and they weren't going to let that pass them by. MandalMotors reached out to the Verpine, the insectoid designers of the B-Wing and V-17 Torrent from the Roche Asteroid Belt (yes, I'm just showing off at this point; yes, I know how pathetic that sounds), to create new hulls, including one of the most durable fighters ever made.

The Bes'uliik was a triangle shaped fighter, with powerful engines and VTOL capabilities, armed with four blaster cannons and two more weapons mounts for anything from missiles, torpedoes, or more cannons. The ships were made of beskar – Mandos could buy ones with full beskar frames and armor, while import models just had the laminate armor – meaning that they almost didn't need shields. They were extremely fast and maneuverable, with a crew of three. Fighter-grade weapons do nothing at all even to the laminate armor, so canon fighters have no chance against one.

Grand Admiral Mitth'raw'nuorodo came from the Unknown Regions of the Galaxy. There the Chiss were the main power, fighting against enemies unlike anything in the "civilized" galaxy. Thrawn's relationship with the Empire meant that the two powers traded weapons and technology, leading to the creation of both the Chiss Star Destroyer and the Nssis -class clawcraft. It used a TIE fighter ball cockpit, with the standard twin ion engines, but that was basically all they used from the TIE. To begin with, they loaded it with a shield generator and a hyperdrive, making it more versatile from the word go.

Instead of the massive solar collection panels, the clawcraft had four "claw" wings extending around the ball of the cockpit, much like an Interceptor. Each claw was armed with a powerful laser (well, technically maser) cannon on the tip and the ship also had an ordinance launcher, using the Chiss equivalent of missiles and torpedoes. The wings each had a series of maneuvering thrusters, making the ship even more agile than any TIE. It was fast, powerful, and maneuverable; an experienced Chiss pilot could fly circles around the aces of the "known" galaxy in canon. Add in the weapons and shields and you have the deadliest fighter in Star Wars Legends.

What Legends fighters do you like the most? Do you think Legends has better fighters or do you think canon has the advantage? Sound off in the comment section below.

articles.title: GTA 6's Loadout System Fixes One of My Biggest Problems With GTA 5, and It's a Massive Upgrade
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Rockstar Games I've never been particularly fond of how Grand Theft Auto 5 handled its ballistics. Being able to carry an entire military surplus store in your back pocket was certainly convenient, but it also removed much of the decision-making behind choosing your equipment. I've always wanted Rockstar to give players a more deliberate approach to building […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google I've never been particularly fond of how Grand Theft Auto 5 handled its ballistics. Being able to carry an entire military surplus store in your back pocket was certainly convenient, but it also removed much of the decision-making behind choosing your equipment. I've always wanted Rockstar to give players a more deliberate approach to building an arsenal.

GTA 6 addresses that with a much more restrictive loadout system and considerably deeper weapon customization. The new approach to weaponry is far more realistic, and while it's Call of Duty's legendary Gunsmith, these changes make the arsenal feel more personal. By adding a new, welcome layer of realism, the weapons if GTA 6 take on their own identities, a big plus for the sequel.

One of my biggest frustrations with GTA 5 was how little consideration its weapon wheel demanded from you. Once you've accumulated enough guns, there was rarely a reason to leave anything behind. Need a shotgun? It's there. Want a sniper rifle? You've got one. Fancy turning an ordinary street encounter into a small-scale military operation? Congratulations, your character apparently has the storage capacity of an aircraft carrier in their back pocket. It's funny in its own way, but it also striped away decision-making that could make combat considerably more engaging. Having access to practically every weapon at all times means there's little incentive to think about your equipment before getting into trouble.

GTA 6 changes that by limiting the active loadout to two sidearms and two longarms. Players still have dedicated slots for melee weapons and explosives, alongside equipment, but the days of carrying an entire armory wherever you go are over. Additional firearms can be stored in the trunk of your personal vehicle or accessed through weapon lockers at Ammu-Nation and other locations. Now, choosing between a shotgun and a rifle actually means something. You can certainly change your selection, but doing so requires a little more consideration than scrolling through an enormous weapon wheel in the middle of a firefight.

I appreciate how this makes your personal vehicle feel like an extension of your character's equipment rather than simply another way to get around Leonida. Having additional firearms stored in the trunk means you're never permanently locked into your initial choices, but you'll need to plan ahead if you want the right tools for a particular job. There's also a greater sense of consequence when carrying weapons around Vice City, since openly displaying a longarm can attract unwanted attention from civilians and police. GTA 6 hasn't taken away the freedom to build an extensive arsenal. It's simply made players think about what they're carrying, and that's a far more interesting approach to combat.

The other major improvement is the attention Rockstar gives to individual weapons. GTA 5 allowed you to modify your firearms, but it was always rather lackluster. Buying a new gun or adding a handful of upgrades was… fine, but there wasn't really a sense of building a personal relationship with a particular weapon. GTA 6 gives you considerably more opportunities to do exactly that. For example, Grand Theft Auto 6 shifts away from generic labels like "Pistol" toward specific fictional brand and model names, which is awesome for giving weapons some personality.

As before, Ammu-Nation is where the customization really comes into its own. You can modify firearms with attachments such as custom grips and magazines, while optics provide another way to tailor a weapon to their preferred approach. Different firearms also have their own performance statistics, giving players more reason to consider how an attachment might affect their setup instead of automatically purchasing every available upgrade. Suppressors and tactical flashlights can even be equipped or removed directly through the loadout, while other modifications require a trip back to Ammu-Nation. It's a welcome degree of flexibility that makes visiting a gun store feel like more than an opportunity to spend money on another firearm.

I wouldn't go so far as to call this Call of Duty's Gunsmith, and Rockstar doesn't need to replicate that system to make its own approach worthwhile. What matters is that GTA 6 gives players more opportunities to shape the firearms they carry, creating a stronger connection between their choices and the weapons they actually use. I want to spend time at Ammu-Nation deciding how my favorite rifle should look and perform, then take it out into Leonida knowing I've made it feel distinctly mine. Combined with the more restrictive loadout system, that extra attention to customization makes GTA 6 's arsenal considerably more satisfying to manage.

Do you prefer GTA 6 's more restrictive loadouts or GTA 5 's massive weapon arsenal? What weapon customization features would you like to see Rockstar add? Let us know what you think in the comments below.

articles.title: Focker In-Law Has A 32% From Critics. Why I Think You Should Ignore That
articles.summary: Or at least consider some other numbers too.
articles.content:
I’ve been looking forward to the release of the Meet the Parents movie, Focker In-Law , all year. However, following its premiere on the 2026 movie schedule , it’s been met with a pretty rough Rotten Tomatoes score of 32%. While that might be a scary number to see, I’m here to tell you I think you should ignore it and focus on some other figures.

At the time of this writing, Focker In-Law’s Tomatometer score is sitting at 32% based on 95 reviews. And when you look at the blurbs from reviews featured on Rotten Tomatoes , they are not complimentary.

Michael Cook from KLRT-TV wrote that while it’s a comedy, “what’s missing are the laughs.” ScreenRant’s Liz Declan thought that the movie wanted to side-step the two sequels that came before it, but “sadly” “offers much of the same.” According to Gabrielle Moss at Collider, there’s “just not much left to milk” here. And Brett Arnold from Yahoo wrote that even though he thinks this is the best Focker film, it still “settles for a low hum of ‘cute enough’ antics.”

Now, I’m always of the opinion that you should make up your mind for yourself with a movie. So, yes, obviously, you should go see Focker In-Law . However, there are also some numbers we can point to that signify there is a group of people who do really like this movie.

articles.title: Blade Runner 2099 Ending: Why Hunter Schafer And The EP Think Fans Will Have Different Feelings
articles.summary: Let the mass speculation begin!
articles.content:
Major spoilers for the Blade Runner 2099 finale, “Share the Fantasy” lie ahead.

Ahead of “Share the Fantasy,” Cora has learned that her adoptive mother, Helena (Sheila Atim) was actually a Nexus-1 Replicant, who was killed by fellow Nexus 1 model Julius (Tom Burke). It turns out the memory belongs to Replicant creator Eldon Tyrell and holds the process of producing the (longer living) Nexus-1s. Olwen and Cora head to an Tyrell Off-World Launch complex, where the former wants to receive more time to live and the latter aims to get the memory back from Julius, who wants the sole power to create Replicants.

Needless to say, the Cora scene – like the finale as a whole – leaves viewers with a lot to chew on. Showrunner Silka Luisa, a longtime fan of the Blade Runner franchise, wouldn’t give any specific answers about the last moment with Cora. However, during her conversation with CinemaBlend, she did acknowledge her thoughts on why viewers would likely have differing thoughts about it:

While 2099 doesn’t have any direct ties to the events of the films, it does indeed follow in their footsteps by providing an ambiguous ending. So I completely agree with Luisa that it’ll spark differing interpretations from viewers. And, just as I probed Luisa for her take on Rick Deckard’s post- 2049 fate , I also directly asked whether Cora would just masquerade as a Replicant moving forward. The EP would only say this to me:

There’s so much to consider in the scene, including the notion that Cora may have actually undergone the Nexus-1 process and become a Replicant herself. Alas, Schafer avoided giving any specifics on that, but she did speak highly of her experience filming the scene and how it differed from much of her time on set:

This show succeeds in delivering impressive visuals , strong performances and brutal action, though I also applaud Silka Luisa and her staff for adding some fresh elements to the franchise. And, while I would love to have some concrete answers regarding the final moments of this limited series, a part of me certainly respects Luisa’s desire to let the audience made up their own mind about the finer details.

articles.title: Robert Downey Jr. Reveals Real Scientist That Inspired MCU Doom, And It's Hilarious
articles.summary: Marvel Studios Robert Downey Jr. is one of the most talented and charismatic performers of his generation, and his about to prove it all over again in Avengers: Doomsday. Downey is returning to the Marvel Cinematic Universe franchise he helped kickstart with Iron Man (2008), only this time, he's masking up to play one of Marvel's most […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Robert Downey Jr. is one of the most talented and charismatic performers of his generation, and his about to prove it all over again in Avengers: Doomsday . Downey is returning to the Marvel Cinematic Universe franchise he helped kickstart with Iron Man (2008), only this time, he's masking up to play one of Marvel's most dangerous and nefarious antagonists, Victor Von Doom (aka "Doctor Doom").

Details of Doom's arc in the film, and details of Downey's performance, have all been kept secret. But as Avengers: Doomsday 's release date approaches, the cast and crew of the biggest Marvel movie ever are saying a bit more about it.

Robert Downey Jr. was part of EW 's in-depth interview with the directors and cast of Avengers: Doomsday and shared a bit more about his take on Doom. According to Downey's breakdown: "This is a guy who is vengeful and capable of doing things, because he’s lost so much that to lose this [battle] would be for all to be lost. He explained that the villain comes with a "scorched-earth vibe," inspired by an unlikely celebrity figure: apparently, RDJ's Doom is based on a "Really crabbed [Neil] deGrasse Tyson . The mechanics that have made every previous Marvel film possible are really what he seeks revenge against. It’s literally like I have contempt for the cosmos as it has been rendered."

That's such a Downey answer, which is to say it's unique and eccentric, but strangely insightful at the same time. Neil DeGrasse Tyson's persona is that of a genius who can articulate major scientific concepts in fun colloquial ways; the other side of that coin has Tyson also offering exasperated debunkings of things like Flat Earth Theory, superhero and sci-fi pseudoscience , or just "correcting" common misconceptions about science or the natural world . That latter part is what Downey seems to be building off for his take on Doom: a genius who is deeply exhausted by the ignorance and ineptitude of those around them – especially those claiming to be "heroes."

That quality is at the core of what makes Doom such a compelling comic character: Doom has actually helped save the world , the cosmos, and reality itself at different points in Marvel Comics lore, not out of any sense of benevolence or justice, but rather because he was the sole person with the will, knowledge, and skill to do it. We have every indication that's going to be his motivation in Avengers: Doomsday , with the added dramatic lure of having Doom desire a new world where the tragedies he's suffered never happened .

The other part of Tyson's persona Downey could be drawing on is his deep knowledge of astronomy and physics, the kind of cosmic mechanics that help one understand how worlds are birthed. Because in the comics, Doom did just that, when he created his own reality, "Battleworld," win the 2015 Secret Wars crossover event – which is in turn inspiring Avengers: Secret Wars , where Downey's Doom is expected to have an equally big arc to play out.

Avengers: Doomsday has a release date of December 18th.

articles.title: Netflix's Darkest Sci-Fi Anime of 2026 Is Already a Masterpiece Worthy of Cyberpunk: Edgerunners
articles.summary: Image courtesy of Sunrise and Shaft Netflix has released a new dark sci-fi anime with all 12 episodes worthy of replacing Cyberpunk: Edgerunners for your Thanksgiving weekend binge. As an original anime series on Netflix, Cyberpunk: Edgerunners delivers a grim story with social inequality as its central driving force. Both seasons explore this notion through different sets of characters as they […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Netflix has released a new dark sci-fi anime with all 12 episodes worthy of replacing Cyberpunk: Edgerunners for your Thanksgiving weekend binge. As an original anime series on Netflix, Cyberpunk: Edgerunners delivers a grim story with social inequality as its central driving force. Both seasons explore this notion through different sets of characters as they navigate the neon-lit streets of Night City, amplified by thrilling sci-fi action. If these are the elements that made you love Cyberpunk: Edgerunners , then Fool Night , with all its episodes already available on Netflix , is here to become a worthy replacement for the anime.

Based on the manga of the same name, the anime is set in a distant future where thick clouds have covered the entire Earth, plunging the world into darkness and cold. With plants naturally dying out, the lack of oxygen continues to increase. Humanity's solution is a procedure called Transfloration, which plants seeds inside people nearing death and transforms them into Spiriflors, plants capable of producing oxygen. This fresh concept is further elevated by a botanical horror premise mixed with crime thriller elements unfolding in this dark world.

The heart of the series is its main character, Toshiro Kamiya, a broke young man who, after a particularly bad night, undergoes the Transfloration process, primarily because he wants the 10 million yen that would allow him to spend the rest of his life eating good food and living happily. However, things don't go as planned, as his money is stolen after the procedure. Nevertheless, Toshiro develops a strange ability to communicate with Spiriflors. This leads him to join a facility investigating the numerous crimes related to Spiriflors, turning the series into a crime thriller in which Toshiro uses his ability to solve various plant-based crimes.

With this foundation, the series begins unveiling the motives behind the various crimes, with each one feeling more human than the last. Meanwhile, the series also follows Toshiro as he takes on duties helping people who want to communicate with the Spiriflors who were once close to them. The result is an emotionally complex exploration of human nature and the motives behind people transforming into plant-like beings, revealing how the grim trade-offs can stem from the most unimaginable circumstances. All the while, the series explores Toshiro's own complicated situation with his mother, which, from the very beginning, makes viewers emotionally invested in him and eager to see him live the remainder of his life to the fullest.

On top of this brilliant premise, the anime is also gorgeously crafted by Sunrise and Shaft, elevating the botanical elements of the series and presenting them exactly as they are meant to feel. This makes the anime one of the most visually appealing series of 2026 as well. All in all, Netflix's Fool Night is a true sci-fi masterpiece that deserves to stand alongside other masterpieces on the platform, such as Cyberpunk: Edgerunners .

"Let Me Sell You a Dream" is also throwback to the types of pseudo anti-yuppie tunes that Talking Heads was known for including 1988's "(Nothing) But Flowers" and 1979's "Life During Wartime". Byrne explains that the Musk end-credits song was arguably the "fastest" he has ever written in his career. A time when Byrne was told by the music industry he was too audacious? How about when he did his first solo album in 1989, the Latino infused "Rei Momo"?

"They implied that I shot myself in the foot and that the fans were going to leave," said Byrne, which if you look at the full houses for his concerts, not to mention the Broadway run of his concert show American Utopia is definitely not the case: His appearance last November at the Dolby Theater drew the likes of Oliver Stone, Judd Apatow and Derek Waters, while his Hollywood Bowl late August appearances for "Who Is The Sky?" were jam packed.

articles.title: Wolverine Is One of Marvel's Biggest Stars, So Why Does His Current Comic Feel So Directionless?
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Marvel Comics Wolverine turned 50 in 2024, with Marvel taking a well-deserved victory lap with the character. Honestly, the chance that anyone looked at the character in The Incredible Hulk #181 and predicted that he would become more popular than Captain America, Iron Man, Thor, Superman, and Wonder Woman is just about nil. Logan went from Hulk […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Wolverine turned 50 in 2024, with Marvel taking a well-deserved victory lap with the character. Honestly, the chance that anyone looked at the character in The Incredible Hulk #181 and predicted that he would become more popular than Captain America, Iron Man, Thor, Superman, and Wonder Woman is just about nil. Logan went from Hulk third wheel to Giant-Size X-Men #1, joining the roster of the team and helping them reach new heights under writer Chris Claremont starting in issue #94. In fact, it's safe to say that the success of the X-Men is tied up with Logan's own popularity. He helped make the anti-hero into one of the most popular types of characters in the industry and one of the most popular characters in pop culture right now, but you'd never know it if you looked at Wolverine (Vol. 8).

This book premiered as part of the X-Men's "From the Ashes" relaunch in 2024 . It's written by Saladin Ahmed, the Eisner Award-winning writer of Black Bolt, Miles Morales: Spider-Man, and Ms. Marvel. Ahmed won for Black Bolt but since then has become more of a workhorse writer than a superstar, putting out good but not great runs on mid-level books. He's a massive Wolverine fan, as he revealed in the letter he wrote readers in issue #1, and has Logan's voice down. Working with artists Martin Cocolo and Julius Ohta, he's pit the ol'Canucklehead against new threat the Adamantine and various classic Wolverine villains Cyber, Lady Deathstrike, Donald Pierce, Romulus, and Sabretooth, with appearances by Post and Mastermind. That seems cool, but there's a problem – the book has no direction.

So, before we get into this, I want to talk about comic publishing in the 2020s. The late '80s saw the rise of the trade paperback, collected editions of comic stories. They would become more and more popular, to the extent that comics started to be written for the trade. This would also change the way comic runs worked; a new creative team would come onboard a book and they would usually start a story that would last until the end of the run. It's basically what people expect from comics nowadays. Sometimes it works, sometimes it doesn't.

When Ahmed started the book, he introduced the Adamantine, a sentient magical metal used by the gods to create magic weapons over the millennia. The opening story introduced the idea that adamantium was basically a bastardized version of the magical metal, one created by humans, and the Adamantine wanted to destroy all of the adamantium to cleanse the world of the "false metal", creating a place where it controlled the most powerful fighters through weapons created from its metal. While I wasn't the craziest about the opening story arc, this was a fine direction for the book.

However, Ahmed did something different. Instead of doing the traditional "writing for the trade", he started to tell other stories. As a longtime Wolverine reader, I got what he was trying to do immediately – he was trying to do Larry Hama-style Wolverine stories. Hama is a legitimate comic legend , the creator of G.I. Joe, and his run on Wolverine (Vol. 2) #31-118 is one of the greatest of all time. Long runs were the thing back then, and Hama did what his compatriot Chris Claremont did to keep the book interesting. Hama would write long arcs that would go in numerous directions but all serve a central idea. So, for example, his first 17 issues of the book were basically getting to know the character and his settings and introducing a focus on the shadows of Logan's past. I ssue #48 began the Weapon X arc of the book , which lasted til about the 60s with a short breather and then we got the bone claws, which turned into the feral arc, where Hama left the book.

Ahmed is basically doing the modern day version of Hama, except he's not really changing the arcs. We've been on the Adamantine for the whole series, with a few other stories here and there like the Mastermind one or the Post one. The next arc looks to be another feral Wolverine arc, or at least a short story, and then there's probably more Adamantine down the road. However, there's just an aimless feeling even to the Adamantine stories. Nothing in the book ever feels like it's actually coming together.

The run does have one throughline, though, but it's not one it needs – nostalgia. Ahmed has been trying to reproduce the work of Hama in numerous ways – we got some bone claws, we got some Sabretooth, we're about to get bestial feral Wolverine. Nostalgia became a huge problem for the X-Men books in the early days of "From the Ashes", but it's one that most of the line doesn't have anymore, as everyone else feels like they have a handle on their books. Ahmed is still all in the nostalgia.

Wolverine is one of Marvel's most popular heroes, but his solo adventures, especially the '90s ones, aren't exactly as well-known. People of my generation have nostalgia for it, but there's been several new generations of Wolvie fans over the years that have no nostalgic relationship to feral Wolverine or bone claw Wolverine. In fact, if I'm being honest, I'm one of the few people I know who thinks the bone claw/feral years are peak; lots of readers hated the noncommital way Marvel did that story. These fans don't want to read directionless nostalgia Wolverine and the proof is in the sales. Wolverine (Vol. 7) was a top 25 seller on every sales chart. This latest one kicked off at number one and then fell down the charts to top 50, and is often lower than that now. This is a huge problem no one is addressing.

As someone who owns a lot of Hama Wolverine (Vol. 2) (I used to own more, but that's a story for another day), I can tell you that above image definitely gives off '90s feral Wolverine vibes, but that's not exactly a good thing. Since Tom Brevoort took over the X-office, we've gotten a lot of nostalgia bait, but here's the thing about that – when Brevoort took over, X-Men '97 was fueling fan nostalgia, so putting out '90s-flavored comics made sense. However, that is no longer case; the second season of X-Men '97 was less '90s focused and also wasn't as huge because it was established, so the X-office moved away from nostalgia.

The problem is that nostalgia is the only direction that Ahmed has right now. He's built his entire run around it, to the extent that even the "main plot" of the run never actually feels like a main plot, it's just a vaguely entertaining story arc that starts and stops all the time. Fans don't want that – we know because the book's sales position has plummeted. Ahmed does a rather good job with the characters at least, so it's not a total bust, but it's also not a book that is going to keep the attention of anyone who doesn't have an encyclopedic knowledge of Hama. However, those of us that do have that can see the run for what it is and that really doesn't help it any either.

What do you think of Wolverine (Vol. 8)? Do you think that its nostalgia focus is working or do you think that it needs something more? Sound off in the comment section below.

articles.title: Channing Tatum Reveals Gambit Movie Plans That Were Closer to Deadpool Than Comics
articles.summary: Channing Tatum's Gambit was very nearly the big-screen superhero that almost wasn't. When the actor finally appeared as the beloved Marvel mutant in 2024's Deadpool & Wolverine, it was not only as a means of bringing the character to life but also to make a giant inside joke for fans familiar with Tatum's long history […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Channing Tatum's Gambit was very nearly the big-screen superhero that almost wasn't . When the actor finally appeared as the beloved Marvel mutant in 2024's Deadpool & Wolverine , it was not only as a means of bringing the character to life but also to make a giant inside joke for fans familiar with Tatum's long history of false starts as Gambit on the big screen. Tatum had flirted with playing with the character long enough that it stretched back all the way to 2006's X-Men: The Last Stand , and persisted for decades, seemingly never to be.

Speaking with Entertainment Weekly about his upcoming reprisal as Gambit for Avengers: Doomsday , Tatum opened up about what the plan was for the Gambit solo movie he was attached to back in the 2010s. According to the star, the idea for the film started out as a romantic comedy in the superhero world, exploring "how do you have a relationship when everybody has superpowers?" That said, Tatum went on to note that plans for the movie shifted as they kept developing it, and as Deadpool became more popular, leading to a "naughty" take on Gambit that didn't happen.

Tatum revealed that the success of Deadpool at the time is what spurred the development of the Gambit movie. As fans may recall, even though Ryan Reynolds' film arrived with half the budget of other X-Men movies, it quickly became the highest-grossing movie in the entire series, even beating the ensemble of X-Men: Days of Future Past , with Deadpool 2 even outgrossing the original by a slim margin.

“We were trying to build a character that was gonna fit in with Deadpool,” Tatum told the outlet. “Deadpool, at that time, was a very specific tone that seemed like it was really hard to work with a lot of other superheroes, in a way, because he would make fun of them. So we were like, ‘Let’s create something that’s a little bit more salacious, a little bit more naughty.’ And Gambit’s a very sexual character anyway, so we definitely were playing around with that.”

Across the years that Tatum developed the movie at 20th Century Fox, it went through a slew of directors, including Rupert Wyatt ( Rise of the Planet of the Apes ), Doug Liman ( Edge of Tomorrow ), and Gore Verbinski ( Pirates of the Caribbean ). At one point, according to reports at the time, Tatum even considered directing it himself, with stories later revealing that Shawn Levy was also in talks at one point, later going on to direct Deadpool & Wolverine .

Given how that movie ended, and the fact that Tatum's presence was at least somewhat a joke, the fan response to his take on the character appears to be what led to him being invited back for Avengers: Doomsday . Though Marvel has already confirmed they're using a deleted scene to explain how he survived The Void, Tatum is quick to note that he still hopes he has a future as Gambit down the line, telling the outlet they wouldn't bring any of the scripts to life they developed at Fox, but adding: "There is a version that does exist that I think is pretty good.”

The one thing potentially standing in Channing Tatum's way of staying on as Gambit for the MCU's future is that Marvel is betting big on the X-Men as their bedrock franchise. Marvel Studios has already confirmed much of the cast for the 2028 X-Men movie, which includes all-new stars and no returning actors from the Fox adaptations. It would be quite surprising if that trend ended with Gambit, especially since the new Rogue actress, Inde Navarrette, is 25 to Tatum's 46. But the odds were stacked against Tatum as Gambit for a decade before, and he beat them once.

articles.title: This Season 2 Survivor Clip Makes Me Miss OG Jeff Probst So Much
articles.summary: Taking me back to the good old days.
articles.content:
It's wild to think about but Survivor has been on the air for 26 years now. The competition series (which is streaming with a Paramount+ subscription ) started its run back in 2000, and longtime fans are still up to date with the current Season 51 . A lot has changed over the years, including Survivor 's prize money , the amount of days the game lasts, and how casting works . I recently watched a vintage clip from back in Season 2, and it totally made me miss OG Jeff Probst .

Honestly, how crazy is this Survivor challenge ? Rather than the standard ones we're used to seeing every season, the above clip shows Jeff asking the cast to jump off a cliff and try to survive floating down rapids with boxes of supplies. It's truly terrifying to watch it play out, especially when you consider that Rodger Bingham had only JUST learned to swim before starting the game.

Seeing this retro Survivor clip also made me miss the OG version of host Jeff Probst. While he's pretty warm and cuddly nowadays, he used to be more of a hard ass. I used to love hearing him throw shade at the contestants, often adding salt to fresh wounds in the process. Seriously, he used to call people or tribes "completely useless" back in the day. This always cracked me up, but nowadays the host/showrunner is more likely to give folks a warm hug.

The streaming business is in flux, and Black Friday deals can help explain it.

It's not hyperbole: Netflix stock has been cut in half from its all-time high. Bundles are proliferating. And Skydance CEO David Ellison has made it clear that a merger of HBO Max and Paramount+ is a question of when, not if.

Black Friday streaming deals are an annual tradition at this point, but given the state of the business, they can also shed light on how the entertainment giants behind them are thinking about the future of their products. articles.summary: Avengers: Doomsday's theatrical debut is rapidly approaching, and for many MCU fans, now is the perfect time to binge watch every film, television show, and press release to try and catch every lore detail or hint as to what's to come. Unsurprisingly, there are a number of Marvel projects that have flown under the radar, […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Avengers: Doomsday 's theatrical debut is rapidly approaching , and for many MCU fans, now is the perfect time to binge watch every film, television show, and press release to try and catch every lore detail or hint as to what's to come. Unsurprisingly, there are a number of Marvel projects that have flown under the radar, and for fans looking to check out everything the multimedia giant has to offer that also happen to enjoy anime, Disney+ has the perfect fix.

Marvel Future Avengers initially premiered in 2017 before making its way to the streaming giant in 2020. The anime original series follows Makoto, Adi and Chloe, three teenagers who were raised and genetically tampered with by Hydra, who have brainwashed the teens to believe that the Avengers are the true evil threatening the planet. The series ran for two seasons with a total of 39-episodes, making the series a relatively easy commitment to watch from start to finish.

Marvel Future Avengers was produced by Studio Madhouse, a major entity within the anime industry that has also produced massive shonen franchises like One-Punch Man , Hunter x Hunter , and Frieren: Beyond Journey's End . The anime was directed by Yuzo Sato, who also worked on the 2010 Iron Man anime that was also produced by Madhouse, as well as having previously worked on Kaiji: Ultimate Survivor and Hunter x Hunter: Phantom Rouge . The series is filled with cameos featuring iconic characters from across the multiverse.

The core avengers that serve as mentors to the leading trio include Iron Man, Captain America, The Hulk and Thor, as well as bringing in Wasp and giving her a main role in the series. They aren't the only supers that make an appearance over the anime's two seasons, bringing in names like Iron Fist, Doctor Strange, Black Panter, Bucky Barnes, Spider-Man and many, many more. While Future Avengers does have its three anime-original leads, the cameos made by the Avengers aren't just used to bait in new audiences.

Each of the heroes introduced throughout the series are used to push the narrative and each of the main trio's character arcs forward, whether it be to help flesh out the world Future Avengers takes place in, tactical back-up in sticky situations, or even to just provide a mentorship role to the main characters. The anime follows Makoto, Adi, and Chloe as they discover that their lives with Hydra have been an elaborate lie, eventually being taken in by the Avengers and acting as apprentices, going on missions and aiding the team in thwarting Hydra's plans.

Each of the main trio's powers are unique as well, with Makoto, the center and "lead" of the group being capable of using "aerokinesis," which allows him to manipulate high-powered winds to disrupt battlefields and can create defensive shields of concentrated air as well as being able to fly. Adi is a "technopath" who is able to innately hack into computer systems and control machines with his mind. Tony Stark provides Adi with a special device and suit that amplifies his capabilities. The female lead, Chloe, is a shapeshifter with powers similar to that of Mystique — capable of replicating the physical form and voice of anyone she sees.

As of writing, there has been no announcement that Marvel Future Avengers will receive a third season . The second season of the anime came to an end in 2018 as the Avengers, accompanied by Makoto, Adi, and Chloe face off against Maximus and his forces. Despite the fact that the anime has no continuation beyond the first two seasons, Marvel Future Avengers did receive a tie-in manga that released alongside the anime from 2017 to 2018 that was later compiled into a 6-chapter volume.

The manga follows the same core premise as Season One of the anime, but condenses some of the story down for those who want to binge the series quickly. But for now, this is the only easily accessible Marvel anime to check out right now. Have you ever seen Future Avengers ? Let us know in the comments.

articles.title: Danny Boyle Said Robert Pattinson Would Make A Great Bond Years Ago. Now He’s Backing An Actor To Be His Villain
articles.summary: Let’s throw some names into the mix!
articles.content:
In 2019, Danny Boyle, who was originally named the director for the James Bond film that eventually became No Time to Die , suggested Robert Pattinson as the man to take over as the next person to play Bond. Now, seven years later, that prediction has come true, as Pattinson was officially named the next 007 last week. Boyle isn’t done making suggestions, however, but now he’s switched to who should play the villain: Jack O’Connell.

O’Connell was one of the (many) actors who were rumored to be in the running for Bond 26 before Amazon MGM and director Denis Villeneuve ultimately decided to go with Pattinson, and I think his take on O’Connell as the villain is also an inspired idea as well. Along with who could be the next “Bond Girl,” the next Bond Villain is another big casting chip that still needs to fall soon before filming kicks off, hopefully in 2027.

O’Connell isn’t the only name being bandied about to play James Bond ’s next villain. Another actor who has worked with Boyle before, Cillian Murphy , has been a popular choice among fans. Barry Keoghan, who worked with Murphy on the 2026 movie schedule in Peaky Blinders: The Immortal Man (which was headed up by Bond 26 writer Steven Knight), is also a top pick. Idris Elba, whom many hoped (including me) could be the next Bond, though even he admitted he’s too old for the role now, is also a common name thrown out there (and honestly, maybe my pick).

Denis Villeneuve says his highly anticipated reboot of the James Bond franchise isn't going to back away from the "unapologetic" traits of the iconic character.

The Dune: Part Three director teased his vision of 007 in a new interview and suggested that he's a traditionalist when it comes to portraying Ian Fleming's suave, seductive, killer spy.

"I love traditions," Villeneuve told Time . "I love the unapologetic way the character behaves, the panache. I’m not here to change the DNA of James Bond. I’m here to embrace it, to bring it to the world of today. I’m a hardcore James Bond fan, and I want other fans to have fun watching my film. Of course, it will be tainted by my sensibility. articles.title: Harry Potter Confirms 1 Book Character Is a Puppet in HBO's Reboot, But That Will Change
articles.summary: HBO HBO's Harry Potter TV series has been clear from the jump that the only reason to reboot the property after eight movies and more than $7.7 billion at the box office is an increased fidelity to the source material. True to their word, plenty of details have been released about the series, including new footage, […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google HBO's Harry Potter TV series has been clear from the jump that the only reason to reboot the property after eight movies and more than $7.7 billion at the box office is an increased fidelity to the source material . True to their word, plenty of details have been released about the series, including new footage, that show they're bringing in characters, set details, and even story points that were excised from the movie adaptations . Now we have an example of the series playing the long game with one character.

In a new post on the official Harry Potter website, details about HBO's show and how it will bring the magical creatures to life arrived this week, confirming that Ron's pet Scabbers will appear, and he'll be a puppet. According to the site, Scabbers is being brought to life in the series as a "startlingly realistic" animatronic that is a "cross-between a soft toy and a robot." A few different versions of Scabbers were created for different scenes across the TV series, pointing out a "sleeping Scabbers" for the Hogwarts Express, but the biggest details is one Potter fans know well, that Ron's rat is missing a toe, just another example of how the show is planning for the future.

The final detail that the Harry Potter website teased about Scabbers in the HBO reboot is "for those of you wondering… He has got that missing toe." Fans of the series know exactly what that means, because Scabbers isn't just an ordinary rat. It's not revealed until the events of Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban , a story that will seemingly be the third season of the planned TV show, that Scabbers is actually revealed to be a human in disguise.

The entire time that Scabbers has been Ron's pet rat, he's actually Peter Pettigrew in his Animagus form, having previously cut off one of his fingers. Prior to the events of the books, Peter is revealed to have been a member of the Marauders, but later joined forces with Voldemort and faked his death as part of an elaborate scheme to frame Sirius Black for betraying Harry Potter's parents, as well as killing several Muggles.

As fans may recall, the seeds for Scabbers being a little different are set up in the first two books, even if it's certainly a surprise when the big reveal happens. To that end, this marks yet another indicator that the HBO Harry Potter series is gearing up for long-term plans, even if we have no idea who will be playing the role of Peter Pettigrew when that batch of episodes finally arrives.

Production on Harry Potter Season 2 is already happening, even with a few weeks left before the series actually makes its premiere on HBO, but that's far from the most distinct indicator that the show is playing the long game. Set photos of Dumbledore star John Lithgow made their way online during the first wave of production, which sparked a rumor that the series may be filming scenes with his character that were actually for much later in the show's plans, since the actor himself is already 79 years old.

One actual confirmation that we have about the show's long-term plans as a series is the show's Forbidden Forest set, which star Nick Frost revealed had been constructed so that it would last for the next ten years, adding: “They’re calling it a living set because it grows as we shoot."

HBO's Harry Potter is scheduled to premiere on Christmas Day.

articles.title: Supremely Scarce Umbreon Pokémon Card Sells for $216,000 at Auction, Nearly 22 Times Its 2025 Price
articles.summary: Image Courtesy The Pokémon Company An eminently rare Umbreon Pokémon TCG card just reached more than $200,000 at auction, adding another enormous six-figure result to an already extraordinary year for Pokémon card collectors. The 2013 Black & White Black Star Promo Umbreon #BW93, graded PSA 10 Gem Mint, commanded $216,000 with buyer's premium during Fanatics Collect's 253rd Weekly auction on […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google An eminently rare Umbreon Pokémon TCG card just reached more than $200,000 at auction, adding another enormous six-figure result to an already extraordinary year for Pokémon card collectors. The 2013 Black & White Black Star Promo Umbreon #BW93, graded PSA 10 Gem Mint, commanded $216,000 with buyer's premium during Fanatics Collect's 253rd Weekly auction on November 22.

Although the Moonlight Pokémon has become accustomed to attracting astronomical prices, this particular result has an interesting wrinkle. Another PSA 10 example sold for $264,000 in September, meaning the latest sale actually fell $48,000 short of the existing record. Nevertheless, that's an extraordinary amount for a card originally distributed in a collection box, particularly considering a Gem Mint example fetched less than $10,000 just last year. With only 14 PSA 10 copies currently recorded, this Umbreon has developed into one of the more formidable (and unheralded) Eeveelution grails of the Black & White era. Let's take a gander at how it got there.

All-Time Record Sale: $264,000 in September 2026

Umbreon #BW93 may lack the widespread recognition of Evolving Skies’ famed Moonbreon Special Illustration Rare or the tremendous cachet of the iconic POP Series 5 Umbreon Gold Star, but the latest auction result demonstrates that collectors are willing to spend an outrageous amount of money for a pristine copy.

According to PSA's sales records , another Gem Mint copy commanded $264,000 through Fanatics Collect on September 28. The November result represents an 18.2% decline from that previous benchmark, which is hardly insignificant when dealing with such an expensive piece of cardboard. Still, $216,000 would have been an almost unimaginable sum for this particular promo just a few years ago. The card's 14-copy PSA 10 population certainly helps explain its appeal, especially as other Black & White-era Pokémon cards have recently commanded similarly staggering prices .

Beyond that, PSA's documented sales history includes a Gem Mint example that sold for just $9,900 on eBay in July 2025. Compared with that transaction, the latest $216,000 auction result represents an increase of $206,100, or approximately 2,082%, in less than a year and a half—nearly 22 times the previous price.

Intriguingly, the September record-setting copy was the very same card that sold for $9,900 in 2025, according to its PSA certification number. The market has clearly undergone a dramatic transformation in a remarkably short period, even if the latest result suggests that prices aren't necessarily destined to climb indefinitely. Given that six exceedingly rare Eeveelution cards combined for nearly $600,000 in an earlier auction this year, Umbreon's latest showing fits rather neatly into a broader pattern of extraordinary demand for Eevee's various evolutions.

Unlike the traditional booster-pack chase cards that dominate many high-end Pokémon auctions, Umbreon #BW93 originated in the Sylveon Collection, which was released on November 15, 2013. This collection box celebrated Sylveon's arrival in the TCG and included four Black & White booster packs, a Sylveon figurine, a Fairy Energy card, and nine promotional Pokémon cards featuring Eevee and all eight of its evolutions.

Umbreon was numbered BW93 and featured a distinctive Cosmos holofoil treatment and artwork credited to the entire The Pokémon Company Art Team (something only 15 other cards can boast). While this illustration had already appeared in Japan during the Pokémon Center's 2012 Eevee Collection campaign, its 2013 English release offered collectors a particularly attractive version of the fan-favorite Dark-type Pokémon, complete with its glowing yellow rings, elegantly mysterious aura, and moody coloration.

We've already witnessed three Southern Islands promos combine for $972,000 at auction , while Umbreon Gold Star's staggering $738,100 sale offers further evidence that collectors have an almost insatiable appetite for Eevee’s Dark-type evolution. Whether this particular Black & White promo eventually surpasses its $264,000 record remains to be seen, but one thing is crystal-clear: Umbreon is perfectly capable of turning a once-modest retail collectible into something worth more than a luxury sedan.
