articles.content:
Dave Keuning , guitarist for The Killers , said that he survived a "major stroke" two weeks ago that had a "40% chance of survival" but he's still able to "play guitar just as good as before." He revealed the news on Thanksgiving, along with announcing the birth of his daughter.

"Happy Thanksgiving, everyone! Three months ago, we had our baby girl, Odette," Keuning wrote. "Two weeks ago, I had a major stroke, and thanks to my wife acting fast, I went straight to the hospital and into surgery. The first hour after a stroke is critical when it comes to getting to the hospital. I had a blood clot in my brain that cut off the blood supply to the entire right side of my brain. By the time I arrived at the hospital, I was blind in one eye and had lost function on my left side, but I still wasn’t able to realize I was having a stroke. articles.title: Record Store Day Black Friday's Most Wanted, 2026: Beatles, Noah Kahan, Bruce Springsteen, Prince, Sombr, Billy Joel, Katseye and Other Vinyl Must-Finds
articles.summary: Record Store Day is back in black. As you likely already know, RSD is a semiannual holiday for vinyl hounds, with the Black Friday edition being a less jam-packed adjunct to the primary event in April — meaning that, this year, for instance, there are "only" 188 titles being released, almost exactly half of the […]
articles.content:
14,500 copies on 4x LP; 3,700 copies on 2x CD; black vinyl

Springsteen buffs will not always agree on favorite individual shows from his and the band's 50-year-plus history, but it's hard to imagine a single fan not considering the "Born to Run" era to be peak form. or not taking a serious interest in this rendering of a long and loose New Year's Eve concert at the close of 1975. The only question might be which physical format you want it in, since Sony is offering it for Record Store Day Black Friday in both LP and CD form. The much greater amount of vinyl pressed indicates an obvious consumer preference for vinyl nowadays, but with a concert this length, some may reconsider whether they want to flip sides seven times to get it all and opt for compact disc. Whether you pick up a vinyl slipcase or CD jewel box, there are succinct but sweet liner notes from Erik Flannigan, who points out that, yes, that is the band (except for Bruce) decked out in tuxedos in the photographs in the packaging. Good thing any formality about this wonderful show ends there.

10,000 copies of vinyl 12-inch EP; Alpenglow-colored vinyl

Kahan's exclusive releases have been among the biggest draws at many recent Record Store Days, which is no surprise, given the ongoing presence of two of his studio albums in the top 10 and stadium tours that sell out instantaneously. Fans will already be familiar with the four songs on this EP — "Lighthouse," "Staying Still," A Few of Your Own" and "Orbiter" — since they first appeared as bonus tracks on a digital deluxe edition of his smash "The Great Divide" album (and "Orbiter" is a proper single). But having the four tracks partitioned off into their own separate physical release will be irresistible to diehard stickheads.

It's not like you're going to get any songs here that you didn't already get on the recent "Rubber Soul" 60th anniversary super-deluxe edition… or, for that matter, that you haven't had access to since 1966. But then, that's the point: This single LP is a recreation of the exact album that U.S. Beatles fans got in '66, down to the original stereo mix. But that's been out of print for a long time… and has never been uin print as a gold-colored record, which is the main novelty here. The good news for Beatles collectors is that it's been pressed in numbers that fall at the very top end of pressings for Record Store Day; the bad news is that 15,000 still won't last long.

9,400 copies on 3x vinyl; 2,700 copies on 2x CD; vinyl color is crystal blue curaçao

The Prince estate is really making the most out of the fact that it had a pro-shot film of Prince's six-month 2006-7 residency in Las Vegas in the can. A film of "3121 Las Vegas Live" will briefly hit the big screen in early December, followed by a Blu-Ray edition for home consumption. In the meantime, if you want a physical manifestation of just the music, Record Store Day participant shops are the place to go. The performance captured here starts at a slow simmer but quickly heats up. Suffice it to say that, after hearing this purely audio version, I'll be lined up for the movie.

Every time there is a new CD boxed set in the ongoing series of Joni Mitchell archival anthologies, a single live performance from that collection gets broken out to have its own separate LP edition for Record Store Day. No complaints at all about that. This '72 concert is all Joni, accompanying herself on guitar, piano or dulcimer, all the way to a closing "Circle Game" that does have her suddenly surrounded by a chorus of famous and unfamous friends. Some will prefer Mitchell in her purest early-ish form here, and some may prefer the big band era that followed. But hearing the purity of that voice with an emphasis on the then-recent "Blue" and then-forthcoming "For the Roses" is a knockout experience. The only thing more you could wish for is a gatefold jacket instead of putting both discs in a single sleeve (the product description promises gatefold, but it's not), or liner notes, but it's still a handsome-looking as well as -sounding package.

The last Billy Joel live album, released for Record Store Day Black Friday 2025, was "Live From Long Island," pressed in a quantity of 1,500 copies — and fans are still pissed about that. (Resale copy prices are not completely exorbitant, but they do go for more than $100.) Fortunately, the record company got the message and is putting three times that many of this followup on sale, 4,600, although that still may not completely sate the market for live Joel. It's a spirited set, from a hyperactive "Angry Young Man" opening forward, recorded Dec. 5, 1976 at Connecticut College for a TV special. It includes 15 never-before-released tracks from either the original live shows or a followup that was done to get better takes for the special. The blurb on the back cover promises that four more tracks will be included in a "Turnstiles" 50th anniversary boxed set coming out next year. But few Joel fans will complain about that wait given the wealth of heretofore unreleased music here.

Sombr: 7,500 copies on silver vinyl

Boone: 5,000 copies on black and white galaxy vinyl

The Sombr and Benson Boone releases are very similar, in that each is a first-time vinyl issue of the EP that started their major-label careers before they broke a lot bigger with a full album that followed. Bot EPs are also mellower than some of the hit music that followed for these artists — Sombr lives up to his name more here. His EP, at four tracks, is less expansive than Boones, which runs to eight songs, and comes with a 12-by-24 insert that has a poster image on one side and lyrics on the other. Apart from their musical merits, both discs just look fab, pulled out of their sleeves and placed into the wild.

Withers: 2,600 copies on LP; 1,300 copies on CD; LP is black vinyl

Various artists/Sweet Relief: 1,200 copies

Now here's an unofficial two-fer anyone should think about picking up and turning into a double feature, even if their simultaneous release, coming from different labels, may be coincidental. First, there's Withers' own 1974 performance, captured for British TV. You can tell the audio is unedited: Withers is heard telling the studio audience that some of his band members are out sick, and in one case restarting a speech. The relaxed feel carries over to the superlative songs. Meanwhile, I have to give an even more enthusiastic endorsement to a double-LP tribute album put together as a benefit for the Sweet Relief Foundation that includes all-new tracks. I was hoping the great Chris Pierce — one of the closest things we have to a modern-day Withers right now — would be one of the artists chosen, and to my sweet relief, he was, contributing "Better Off Dead." There are also choice cuts from Rickie Lee Jones, Lady Blackbird, Marilyn McCoo and Billy Davis Jr., Ben Harper and others who know how to mix their own spin on things with takes that feel faithful to Withers' vibe.

2,600.copies of six-LP boxed set; multiple vinyl colors

Rhino has gotten in the habit of issuing one complete boxed set per RSD event for a renowned artist from the Warner-Elektra catalog of riches, from John Prine to Devo. This one for 10,000 Maniacs, composed of all the albums the group put out before Natalie Merchant split to go solo in 1993, is being seen by fans as a very necessary corrective to the fact that a lot of that stuff has been out of print on vinyl forever. Four studio albums are joined by the pre-fame compendium "Hope Chest" and a newly assembled rarities disc full of delectable covers. Merchant is credited with helping oversee the package, including the design of the physical elements, although the liner notes (which are very good) do not include interviews with her or any of the bandmates who continue to carry on without her. It's worth noting that all of the albums included except the rarities LP are due to be issued individually early next year, if it's just one or two you need to pick up. But as a fan from their earliest major-label days, I couldn't imagine not getting the whole thing right now. A matter of curiosity: All of the box and LP packaging here changes the band's name to Ten Thousand Maniacs from 10,000 Maniacs (although the numerical usage pops up in the liner notes). Some elements of the album cover art have been changed, along with the band-name logos — it has to be a Merchant thing. But if you pick up the individual issues in a few months, apparently the name and artwork will be as we remember them. (The fact that the albums in this box have different covers is further cemented by the lack of barcodes.) Those peculiarities aside, t's a great trip down maniacal memory lane.

Jepsen has been nothing but prolific in this era, first issuing "Day and Night" as a hefty double-album, then adding eight additional tracks onto the original 24 for a deluxe edition, "Day and Night (Continued)." that runs to an hour and 55 minutes of material. Some things may be more easily digested in smaller chunks, of course, and this EP — also titled "Day and Night (Continued)" — breaks out those eight fresher tracks and gives them their first appearance in a physical format. Plus, you get still more from her photo shoot at Eagle Rock's Casa Bianca, the best pizza joint in L.A., and if that's not reason enough to pick it up, you've got eight more.

The previous RSD exclusive editions of the "Wicked" and "Wicked: For Good" sold out so quickly, I never did actually catch a glimpse of either of them in my many store visits. That will probably prove true for this combined set that packages both soundtracks together in a 4-LP set in a slipcase with a poster. (The track list, if accurate as rendered online, leaves out the bonus track that was added onto the original RSD "Wicked" issue.) Good luck hunting this down, unless it turns out every franchise fan was sated by the previous two releases after all, which isn't likely. It's gonna be popular.

3,300 2x LP copies; black vinyl

The first of several releases we'll mention here produced by "jazz detective" Zefv Feldman is a welcome incursion into the wonderful world of Blakey. It comtbines two previously unreleased performances in Paris, the first from 1963 and sporting famous players like Freddie Hubbard and Wayne Shorter, the second with a different ensemble in '68. "Moons" were on the band leader's mind, as the collection includes the two big musical moon shots of the era, "Blue Moon" and "Moon River." The latter opens the collection and might give Henry Mancini a heart attack if he were still around to have one — it's like "Moon River" on amphetamines (not speaking literally, friends, just figuratively), and it's quite a fantastic flood. The liner notes booklet is copious as with almost any Feldman-related release, and even though a CD edition will follow for the general market in a week, it's always worth picking up the limited-edition vinyl versions of these releases just for the larger type and photographs. And, sure, the wide-open grooves, too.

5,000 copies of 2x LP; on “Third Pyramid Pink” vinyl

I would have taken an interest in a B-52s live set anyway, but this one turns out to be particularly a wowser because of the addition of a three-man horn section that really helps some of the songs rock in an augmented way. Fans may already know this Roseland Ballroom NYC '82 performance from when it was included in the "Ancient Culture: Mesopotamia Revisited" set, but for those of us who didn't have that, or anyone who did but just likes a good breakout, it's a delightful revelation of the band at its early '80s peak.

3,500 copies of 12-inch vinyl EP; red vinyl

Cher had not released any original material in many years until she came back with a Christmas project that included some songs newly written to add to the holiday tuneage canon. With this EP spinoff, the emphasis is on the dance-ier chestnuts, including three different mixes of "DJ Play a Christmas Song" and an added duet with Kelly Clarkson. The lady-in-red cover shot is different from any previous artwork in her Christmas-music campaign, too.

2,600 copies of 2x LP; black vinyl

Another archival production from Zev Feldman, who is stretching out from being seen as "just" a jazz guy with his Bobby Womack and Marianna Faithful releases this Record Store Day. Womack can also stretch out, as it turns out, with two numbers in this live set that go past the 12-minute mark, "You're Welcome, Stop on By" and "Communication" are both over 12 minutes long. Recorded in Paris in 1976, where the liner notes say he was having a higher profile at the time than in the U.S., this collection feels essential as a revelation of just what an expansive showman he was as well as crafter of classic soul singles.

Sax man Getz is the only one with his name above the title on this release, but for the first three of its six sides, legendary guitarist João Gilberto is his equal costar. Together, they recreate the magic they'd made together in a historic studio teaming in one of the few live shows they did together to follow that. All the music here was previously released by Resonance more than a decade ago, but this three-LP set for the first time combines two albums — one of Getz with Gilberto in SF, one without — into an exemplary single package (and the Getz-only half of the equation never made it onto vinyl before). The multiple interviews or essays in the copious liner notes even include a sizable explanation of the bossa nova craze that finds a kind of quiet culmination here.

5,000 copies of single-sided EP

We were not able to preview this particular release, so we cannot vouch for what the "dance break" versions of three of Katseye's most popular songs sound like — "Debut," "Gnarly" and "Gabriela." But we can tell you the way it will fly off the shelves will be gnarly indeed. All three mixes are congregated on one side of the vinyl, with a mystery etching on the other. Each copy is said to includes two out of six "randomly selected unique photocards," so fans will be figuring out how to get around the one-copy-per-customer rule in most stores, as if this needed an incentive to sell out faster.

This is the "Bitches Brew"-era Miles who took free jazz into the land of psychedelia, if you hadn't already guessed that from the cover art by his favorite cover painter in the '60s, Mati Klarwein. It might as well have been recorded at the Fillmore, even though Davis actually had his all-star quintet (Wayne Shorter, Chick Corea, Dave Holland and Jack DeJohnette) in Copenhagen for a TV taping. The music has previously been heard on a DVD and on a one-time vinyl pressing of just a few hundred copies, but this mastering is said to be a revelation even for the relatively small number of cultists who've already heard this dynamic performance in some form.

10,000 copies; "Derpy Sussie Splatter" vinyl

The hunt for "Kpop Demon Hunters" collectibles never stops. Record Store Day just had dual editions of the soundtrack that were quick and easy sellouts, but that could hardly stand in the way of yet another version — and surely not the last — this one featuring fresh art created by official "Demon Hunters" production designer Mingjue Helen Chen and visual development artist Marion Bordeyne. We'll let the product description do the rest of the talking: "This Derpy Sussie Splatter vinyl includes exclusive holographic art on both the front cover and triple gatefold, 3 of 6 mini inserts, 1 of 3 holographic mini inserts, a sticker sheet, and an oversized poster." You might have to take their word for it since it won't be surprising if most or all of the copies are gone by the time you get your lazy post-Thanksgiving butt to the shop.

1,800 copies on three-sided 2x LP set; black vinyl

We're still morning Faithful's passing, so it's moving to hear her in her prime, or one of her primes, in a performance captured in 1983, after a comeback run of three acclaimed albums on Island, including of course "Broken English." The tape of the D.C. set ends with the title track from that latter album and is missing a few final songs from the actual performance, so it's spread across three sides and the fourth is devoted to an etching of a William Blake quote in concentric-circle script.

Fountains of Wayne's final album before their breakup sometimes gets undervalued because it's their least comical, most sober outing, perhaps reflecting the more dominant influence of Chris Collingwood, versus the wryer touch favored by Adam Schlesinger, who'd run the show more on the preceding record. Regardless, there's wit enough here, along with some of the band's starker songs. It's been challenging for FoW fans to complete their vinyl collections, since this fast went out of print after a single pressing in 2001. Even now, 2,000 is not a lot, but it'll be at least enough to satisfy some of us who never stopped believing that this brilliant group had it going on.

As the title and cover hint, this is a collection of cover songs these Dolls have done over the years, and what great taste they've had in other bands, as evidenced in a collection that runs from the Plimsouls' "A Million Miles Away" to the Kinks' "Catch Me Now, I'm Falling," with stops for Tom Petty, INXS, Prince and… Supertramp! (A CD and digital release will follow a week after this vinyl exclusive.)

We did not get a review copy of this, but we're going to guess from the product description alone that it might be fun, with or without actually listening to what's in the grooves, just from looking at them. "Zoetrope" discs have been a thing for a while, turning vinyl into animation, but this is the first one we can recall seeing that is billed as a 3D zoetrope disc, with cardboard glasses to put on to enjoy the effect. We look forward to hearing whether the effect of watching that is as mind-bending as the Gizzard boys' music typically is, and what substances it is best combined with.

2,215 copies of six-45-rpm-singles boxed set; different marbled color variations

Jazz Dispensary dispenses something worth picking up for every single RSD edition, and this time they've eschewed the usual single-LP compilation format to put out a box of singles. It comes in a candy-style box, with six different vintage singles in different but equally delicious-looking colors, plus some glow-in-the-dark 45 adapters as a bonus. As usual, even though the description calls these "jazz," the music therein leans more toward the funk side of the fence, from Eddie Jefferson's honestly groovy "Psychedelic Sally" to Patrice Rushen's kinda-weird "Kickin' Back." Obscure but charming singles from Rusty Bryant, Idris Muhammad, Pleasure and Johnny Hammond are also represented. Will you play these a lot, or easily find shelf space for an odd-shaped package? Probably no in both cases, yet it's kind of irresistible as a hep novelty package nonetheless.

What could be better for celebrating the season than NRBQ's 1978 "Merry Christmas From NRBQ" EP? Very possibly, a modern expansion of that project that extends it to 19 tracks, 10 of them making their vinyl debut, one (the closing "Auld Lang Syne") getting its premiere altogether. We weren't able to preview this package to tell you whether they do or don't rock out the newly added "Jesus Loves Me" and "The Christmas Song," but we hope to score a copy and fill in that part of the NRB-FAQ.

articles.summary: Thank goodness she did this!
articles.content:
Florence Pugh is one of the biggest movie stars we have right now. I mean she’s in both films bearing the Dunesday nickname on the 2026 movie schedule for crying out loud! So, I’d expect a director to move mountains in order to get her on their film. It turns out Pugh had balls of steel even before she earned her A-list status. When she was just 22, she was faced with the ultimate Sophie’s Choice of movie roles.

This, ladies and gentleman is yet another reason why Florence Pugh is the major name she is. She clearly understood at the time that she had stumbled onto two incredible parts, and she didn't want to choose, despite others telling her she must. With that in mind, she pushed aside any fears and decided to simply ask for what she wanted. Here’s what happened next, per her interview with Elle :

Pugh ended up shooting Midsommar first with writer/director Ari Aster, which proved to be a taxing shoot for the actress . It was all worth it because the A24 film has since become known as one of the best horror movies of all time , with Dani’s May Queen and the Bear also becoming a popular Halloween costume, too. Pugh later also got a Midsommar tattoo to immortalize the movie on her body.

Right after she made Midsommar in Hungary, Pugh ventured to Massachusetts to make Little Women with writer/director Greta Gerwig alongside a cast including Timothée Chalamet, Saoirse Ronan, Emma Watson , Laura Dern and Meryl Streep . articles.title: Dune 3 Director Breaks Silence on Avengers: Doomsday Releasing the Same Day, "I Was Deeply Disappointed"

The other film is Dune: Part Three, director Denis Villeneuve's highly anticipated finale to the Dune movie trilogy. Fans quickly gave Friday, […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Avengers: Doomsday has been dominating the headlines all week, and largely overshadowing the fact that it is but one of two of the biggest movies of the year releasing on the same day. The other film is Dune: Part Three , director Denis Villeneuve's highly anticipated finale to the Dune movie trilogy. Fans quickly gave Friday, December 18th the unofficial nickname of "Dunesday," and there are many who are hoping it will be the next double-feature cultural phenomenon like "Barbenheimer" (the same-day release of Barbie and Oppenheimer ) in 2023 . However, that's not the way that Villeneuve feels about it.

In a new interview with TIME , Denis Villeneuve expresses his own "disappointment" with Marvel Studios' decision to stand on the release date for Avengers: Doomsday . Read below to find out why.

When asked how he feels about the shared release date between Dune: Part Three and Avengers: Doomsday , Villeneuve basically explains that intentionally or not, Marvel has triggered some level of his trauma from making and releasing these Dune movies.

"Listen, I will be honest. The first Dune came out at the end of the pandemic. We made a great box office in a very rough environment. But we had the winds against us. Then the second movie, same thing. We were meant to release in the fall, and we had to release at the end of winter because of the two Hollywood strikes. We had success, but it was not easy," Villeneuve said. "The third time, I said to myself, 'Finally, there is no pandemic, no strike in sight. We will have a normal release.' Then Disney put the biggest franchise of all time against us. I’m no fool. Those movies are a mammoth. So I was deeply disappointed."

Many would probably agree that Villeneuve has a valid point: The first two Dune films definitely had their respective releases thrown off by the two biggest hits to the entertainment industry this decade: the 2020 Pandemic, and the 2023 Hollywood Strikes. And, to the credit of Villeneuve and Dune, both films did well at the box office (a combined $1.14 billion against a total budget of $355 million), and launched a (moderately) successful HBO spinoff series, Dune: Prophec y (Season 2 premiering in 2027), and won a combined 8 Oscars for its technical and stylistic achievements. A third film was well-earned – as was the chance for the franchise to enjoy at least one normal release date window.

Instead, like the pot of Dune: Part Three , there will be a massive battle for the throne (box office), with both Marvel and Warner Bros. careening toward incursion. Dune Part: Three has already achieved a key strategic victory over Avengers: Doomsday : securing the IMAX premium format.

"We had committed to this date, to IMAX. It was impossible to move. So I accepted my fate, praying to the gods of cinema," Villeneuve continued. " Dune is not a mammoth like the Avengers, but it’s a sexy little animal that has a lot of firepower, and I hope we will survive. It could be one of the biggest box-office weekends of all time because of both movies. Am I in competition with the Avengers? Absolutely not. It’s a T. rex. But I stand proud because I think the film delivers."

Speaking personally, I think both Denis Villeneuve and Avengers: Doomsday director Joe and Anthony Russo will all end up toasting champagne (perhaps even together?) at the end of opening weekend. I will one-hundred-percent be seeing both films, possibly more than once in subsequent weeks of release. Both films are major cinematic events that represent the end of major chapters in cinema, and there is so much overlap in the primary fanbases of both films that it their releases will become a "Barbenheimer" cultural event, guaranteed.

We'll all be watching how the box office battle plays out when Dune: Part Three and Avengers: Doomsday are released on December 18th.

articles.content:
When Saturn Risin9 auditioned for Jordan Firstman’s “ Club Kid ,” her face was still swollen from facial feminization surgery. The musician, DJ and nightlife fixture, who had undergone the procedure a month earlier in April 2025, hadn't even attempted to put on a wig since her surgery. Unable to bring herself to let anyone into her apartment, she played all three characters in her self-tape.

“I think they were just like, ‘Who is this crazy lady?’” Risin9 recalls with a laugh. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Samantha Morton to Receive BFI Fellowship

Firstman, a longtime friend from the nightlife circuit, had told Risin9 at a party two years earlier that he was writing a role for her. But the audition request came just weeks after her gender-affirming surgery. For Risin9, the timing felt like an affirmation — "I thought it was so aligned, at the moment that I was so authentic with myself, that the world opened up to me," she says.

Now, Risin9 is one of the breakout stars of Firstman's A24 comedy-drama, which follows a New York City party promoter whose life is upended by the arrival of a son he never knew he had. As Saffron, a DJ with a protective streak and diva sensibilities, Risin9 brings to the film two decades of experience navigating underground nightlife.

The Bay Area native grew up performing in theater productions and wrote her first play at 11, but turned her attention to music in her 20s after finding that the acting roles available to her didn't align with her identity. She built a career as an independent recording artist, DJ and performer, touring internationally before relocating to Los Angeles in 2017. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Perhaps most gratifying to Risin9 has been the film's reception among audiences far removed from the world it depicts. After a screening at Telluride Film Festival, she was approached by a father who was crying in the arms of his daughter. "I was like, 'Are you okay?,'" she recalls. "And he was like, 'Your movie was just so beautiful.'"

Even Risin9's mother, who has historically been less comfortable watching queer intimacy on screen, ("She likes to pretend that she can't watch people make out and I'm like, 'I think you just don't want to see gay stuff') came away a fan.

The film's success also comes at a particularly exciting moment for queer cinema. In addition to "Club Kid," stories centered on gay men — such as "Elsinore," "La Bola Negra" and "Artificial" — dominate awards season buzz this year. "These films exist in a post-'Heated Rivalry' moment during which audiences seem newly open to queer stories," Variety's Dan D'Addario wrote last month, posing the question: is this the gayest Oscar season ever? "These films launch into surprising directions, showing many different sides of the gay experience."

Risin9 similarly describes this era as the "de-'Will & Grace’-ification of queer art,” in which LGBTQ stories are increasingly afforded the complexity, specificity and messiness that Hollywood has long granted their heterosexual counterparts. "Straight people want to see more things that they don't know about," she says. "We all want to learn. We don't want to stagnate."

Below, Risin9 talks about her audition process, her evolving relationship with nightlife and teaching her young co-star Reggie Absolom to DJ:

Léa Seydoux told me that she loved me in “Club Kid.” She just comes up to me and goes “I love you in the movie,” and I was like, “You saw ‘Club Kid’?” She was like, “I loved it,” and we actually walked the red carpet for “Gentle Monster” in Cannes. So it was kind of a kismet moment.

She had that knowingness that she was giving me something. You know what I mean? Like, “I have to tell you this, and you're gonna live for it.” It was so cute.

I didn't want to be too aware of what was happening because something that I love about acting is letting go and finding that space where you know the rhythm of it and you know what your cues are, but you're also allowing for the character to be thinking and to be human instead of just waiting to perform. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The first scene that we shot was the one where we go to Peter’s [Firstman's] house and find out that he has Arlo, and we're all busting in the house. I was supposed to say a few words about convincing him to do this party — and I was saying it so big, and Jordan just goes, "Just say it.” And I was like, “Oh, okay.”

That was what Jordan's direction always was. It was a lot of trust, but also the encouragement to be comfortable in it and not to be so showy.

Jordan and I were very friendly party friends. We've always had a really good rapport, and we hung out once in Atlanta. I brought my little cousin with me and I'm very protective of my family. I'm the disciplinarian. So I think he got to see that outside of the "most fun girl at the party," I’m also this maternal, super supportive figure. And I think his wheels started to turn.

I saw him about two years later at a party, and he was like, “Hey, I wrote this movie and I wrote a role for you. Would you be in my movie?” It's like 5 a.m. So I'm like, “Yeah, girl, whatever.” You know how many people stop me at the end of the night and say, “Oh my God, it would be so cool if we did this?”

I showed up in a fully laced bodysuit, thinking that they wanted to see a club diva. So I'm in this lace bodysuit at 10 a.m. in Hollywood. And I thought they wanted one of those nasty girls. I was reading it kind of cunty.

And then at the end, Carmen Cuba, our casting director, was like, “Can you do it more empathetic?” And I was like, “Okay, that's me! Let's talk. Let's go.”

There's a line in the movie where it's like, “When's the last time you saw a kid?” And I was like, really, actually, when was the last time I saw a kid? Because I also didn't know if he knew trans people. I was in my head. The last time I saw a kid, the kid was bullying me. So I was like, “Whoa!” Kids can be scary. Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google One of the MCU 's biggest criticisms is that so many of its movies share a similar narrative structure, sense of humor, and tonal balance. Films like Iron Man and The Avengers have ensured that the influence of filmmakers like Jon Favreau and Joss Whedon, respectively, is felt long after they’ve vacated the director’s chair. After all, in many respects, the MCU’s true auteur is Kevin Feige himself, who has overseen the MCU and whose time working on Marvel movies dates back to the original X-Men in 2000. But every once in a while, a filmmaker has brought such a clear vision to a project that it unmistakably bears the trademarks of their other films.

James Gunn is absolutely one of the biggest examples of this. Before Guardians of the Galaxy , Gunn had only directed a pair of very dark, very R-rated genre films in 2006’s Slither and 2010’s Super . And it is Gunn’s storytelling voice and more unconventional sensibilities that made his work with Marvel stand out, to the point that so many people (including his Guardians cast) stood by him after his short-lived firing from Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3 . Even now, years after Gunn left Marvel, the MCU carries much of his creative stamp. Avengers: Doomsday may be the ultimate example of Gunn’s impact on the MCU.

Let’s consider the little that we know for sure about Avengers: Doomsday . The film — directed by Joe and Anthony Russo — serves as the first Avengers film since Avengers: Endgame , it sees not just one but multiple teams from throughout the multiverse unite against a common threat. The Avengers led by Sam Wilson, the New Avengers led by Yelena Belova, the Wakandans, the Fox X-Men, and the newly minted MCU Fantastic Four will all inevitably cross paths, face off against each other, and ultimately unite to prevent Doctor Doom from realizing his mysterious plan. In part, this sounds like a bit of Avengers: Infinity War . But boiled down to its essence, the story sees a group of misfits forced to overcome their petty differences and come together by truly becoming a team.

That sounds an awful lot like the found family theme Gunn employed to spectacular effect in Guardians of the Galaxy , its sequels, and 2021’s The Suicide Squad . The biggest difference is that, instead of a group of five individuals with their own motivations and paths, Avengers: Doomsday expands that out into five teams of heroes. Granted, 2012’s The Avengers and 2025’s Thunderbolts* tread some similar ground in their team-building narratives. But Gunn has made found family one of his trademarks, and arguably few people in current superhero cinema do it better than him.

It says a lot about Gunn’s contributions to the MCU that so much of Marvel Studios' recent output resembles his work, which makes sense since it looked unlikely he would return to Marvel anytime soon. Of course, Gunn’s recent departure from DC Studios raises the possibility that he might return to working within the MCU. After all, he initially ended up working with DC on The Suicide Squad after Disney fired him from Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3 . So it stands to reason that he might hop back over to the other side of the street once his time at DC concludes. Right now, it’s unclear if 2027’s Man of Tomorrow will be the final DC project he works on before he leave.

If that’s the case, Marvel might be able to get Gunn involved in any number of upcoming projects. Both he and Marvel seem to be in no rush to make another Guardians of the Galaxy film, despite star Chris Pratt's interest . Reportedly, the next few years of the MCU will center on the Mutant Saga, and if there’s any Marvel property that feels ripe for Gunn to apply his particular brand of found family superheroes to, it’s the X-Men. It’s challenging to predict which project best to mark Gunn’s potential MCU return, since so little is known about what’s next. But he should absolutely be in the mix to play in the X-Men sandbox.

Should James Gunn return to the MCU? If so, which project should he take on? Let us know your thoughts in the comments!

Avengers: Doomsday arrives in theaters on December 18, 2026.

  Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google LEGO Black Friday deals are live, and there are so many delightful things to see that it truly feels like Christmas morning for LEGO fans. From the launch of Godzilla to all the gifts you can get with your purchases, not to mention the opportunity for LEGO Insiders to earn 4X points, there are so many deals to take advantage of.

LEGO's Black Friday sale kicks off November 27 and runs through November 30, and you can earn three gifts during the sale. The first is the Godzilla Logo and Footprint (40888), an exclusive gift that comes with the purchase of Godzilla . Featuring 359 pieces, measuring 3.5 inches high, 9.5 inches wide, and 5 inches deep, and intended for builders 18 and up, this set is a perfect complement to the mighty kaiju. The footprint matches Godzilla's foot exactly, and the bright blue letters have a Hollywood feel.

The second gift with purchase is the Retro Jukebox (40914), which you get when you spend $250 or more. It has 287 pieces, measures 5.5 inches high, 3 inches wide, and 2 inches deep, and is intended for builders aged 18 and up. The jukebox features a record that spins, and it opens to reveal a smaller jukebox and a minifigure.

The last gift with purchase is the Winter Snow Globe (40918), which you'll get free when you spend $170 or more. This delightful holiday build contains 231 pieces, measures 3.5 inches high, 4 inches wide, and 4 inches deep, and is intended for builders 10 years old and up. Featuring a Christmas tree that spins, a snowman with a hat and scarf, and presents, it's a charming addition to any LEGO collection.

Speaking of Godzilla , the iconic movie monster makes its big debut today on LEGO.com. Godzilla's stature is appropriately huge at over 27.5 inches tall (with heat ray) and features 5,363 pieces, making this an advanced build for those 18 years old and up. With an attachable tongue and heat ray, you can pose this fearsome beast's arms, fingers, tail, and head to capture its most memorable on-screen moments.

Several Star Wars LEGO sets on sale will be retired at the end of the year, so there's no better time to add them to your collection. We have a complete list of all of the Star Wars sets being retired on December 31 you can check out.

Along with the Star Wars sets on sale, there's also a collectible book, several plushes, and a few keychains on sale worth checking out.

Amazon has a lot of deals on Star Wars sets that LEGO.com does not, so make sure you swing by to check these out if you're trying to fill out your Star Wars LEGO collection. Some of them are at the lowest prices we've ever seen them at, or the lowest price in 90 days, like the SMART Play: Luke's Landspeeder set.

The LEGO Black Friday deals have quite a few sets below $50, making them ideal for gift-giving. These are our top picks in that price range.

When does Black Friday start and end? LEGO's Black Friday sale starts on November 27, 2026, and "Black Friday Weekend" ends on Cyber Monday, November 30. LEGO says its offers last through the weekend while stocks last. Popular sets and free gifts can sell out early, so it's best to shop sooner.

Is LEGO cheaper on Black Friday?

Often, yes, but where you shop makes a difference. LEGO.com focuses on exclusives and free gifts, while stores like Amazon usually have bigger price cuts. Amazon started early LEGO Black Friday deals with up to 50% off select sets.

Do I need to be a LEGO Insider to get Black Friday deals?

You don't need to be a member to shop the sale, but joining is worth it. LEGO Insiders is free to join, and members earn points on every purchase that they can spend on members-only rewards, discounts and gifts. You'll need an account to earn points on your Black Friday order.

Where can I find the best LEGO Black Friday deals?

For gifts and new launches like Godzilla, shop LEGO.com or a LEGO Store. For the biggest discounts on existing sets, check Amazon, Walmart, and Target, which often drop LEGO prices further than LEGO does. We'll keep this page updated with the best prices we find through Cyber Monday.

articles.title: How The Family Of Breaking Bad’s RJ Mitte Paid Tribute To The Late Actor On Thanksgiving
articles.summary: Mitte's family continue to mourn the actor.
articles.content:
The holidays are a great time to be around family and celebrate their company, but they are always more difficult when you’ve just lost a loved one. Breaking Bad cast member RJ Mitte died on October 12, 2026, at the age of 34 by suicide. The loss is still fresh for his mother and sister, and they took some time to publicly pay tribute to him on Thanksgiving.

Mitte’s mom shared a photo of herself with RJ Mitte and his sister Lacianne Carriere. She wrote that she’s “missing” him on Thanksgiving, but she “made all [his] favorites”. RJ’s sister also took to her Instagram account to share a throwback photo with the late actor. Here it is:

RJ’s younger sister expressed that she’s “thankful for the time” she had with her brother, and is really feeling his absence on the first holiday she and her family are spending without him. About a month ago, Carriere took to the platform to share a long tribute to RJ, calling him her “everything” and “other half”. It’s a particularly huge loss for his closest relatives.

Mitte’s body was found by his mother on the morning of October 12 in his home in Brownville, Texas. His official cause of death was ruled a suicide the same day. His mother said she had offered and suggested her son go to therapy in the three months before his passing, but he said he was “OK” and “handling it” (via Today ).
